start_here: Keep your rules first, then switch on the every-ten-minutes wake of workflow:stop-programs-left-running with store {"where": "the person's own database", "language": "SQL (PostgreSQL)", "credential_name": "the-persons-database-connection"}. From then on, every ten minutes, a program your left-behind rows describe and no never-stop row names is asked to end, each stop is kept as a program_stops row, and you are told once per sweep that stopped anything.
no_lists_because: It names no list: its rules and its stops are rows of two tables in the person's own database, program_rules and program_stops, which its first steps make when they are missing, read and written with run-sql.
instructions: 1. Keep at least one never-stop row and one left-behind row in your own database, each one program_rules row: id, kind never-stop or left-behind, and rule (the rule as JSON). The first sweep makes program_rules and program_stops when they are missing, and refuses until a never-stop row is there. A never-stop row is {id, why, command_pattern and/or name_pattern}, like {"id": "the-model-proxy", "why": "Every AI session on this computer talks through it", "command_pattern": "model-proxy"}; name every program that must never be stopped, such as the programs your AI sessions talk through and the program that keeps them running. A left-behind row is {id, why, parent_pid and/or session_owner_gone, older_than_minutes, command_pattern and/or name_pattern, and optionally cpu_share_at_least}, like {"id": "shell-loop-left-by-an-ended-session", "why": "A shell a closed session left behind, still busy", "parent_pid": 1, "session_owner_gone": true, "older_than_minutes": 60, "cpu_share_at_least": 0.5, "command_pattern": "^/bin/sh -c "}. With no never-stop row the sweep refuses.
2. Grant tool:list-running-programs read-processes, and tool:stop-programs-left-running read-processes and close-apps, on this computer.
3. Switch on the every-ten-minutes wake of workflow:stop-programs-left-running with your store: the command line's schedule on, naming workflow:stop-programs-left-running and every-ten-minutes.

4. Read each notice when it comes, and the program_stops rows for every stop: outcome ended, still-running, already-gone, not-the-same-program or not-allowed. A program kept by a never-stop row is never stopped, and a program whose session still has an owner is always kept.

worked_examples.title: One sweep stops a shell a closed session left looping
worked_examples.ask: Run the left-running sweep once now with my database.
worked_examples.given: One program: pid 4242, parent 1, its own session, started three hours ago, two hours forty of processor time, command "/bin/sh -c while true; do run-tests; done"; the rows {"id": "shell-loop-left-by-an-ended-session", "why": "A shell a closed session left behind, still busy", "parent_pid": 1, "session_owner_gone": true, "older_than_minutes": 60, "cpu_share_at_least": 0.5, "command_pattern": "^/bin/sh -c "} and {"id": "the-model-proxy", "why": "Every AI session on this computer talks through it", "command_pattern": "model-proxy"}.
worked_examples.hands_back: choose picked pid 4242 by shell-loop-left-by-an-ended-session (cpu_share 0.89); stop asked it to end and it ended; one program_stops row program-stopped:4242:<its start> was kept; one notice "Stopped 1 program left running" was told.
